Thank you for that information. To better understand your symptoms, can you tell me if your hand tremors occur primarily at rest or when you are trying to perform an action, such as reaching for a cup?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete_Blood_Count: WBC 7,500 /μL, Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 230,000 /μL; Thyroid_Function_Tests: TSH 2.5 mIU/L, Free_T4 1.2 ng/dL

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances. This is only for study purposes, so you do not need to list warnings or many alternatives. Please just provide the best final answer.

speaker: Doctor
text: That resting tremor combined with soft speech (hypophonia), reduced facial expressions (masked facies), and cognitive decline strongly points to Parkinson's disease. To confirm the diagnosis, I need to see if there is an asymmetry in your reflexes and motor response; please raise your arms forward and open/close your eyes tightly. DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease
